properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL (Anthony, 2026-10-12, thinking out loud, continuing dec:idea-how-does-the-site-show-what-reflow2-is-for-one-design-by-itself).

His words: "What I'm trying to solve is that I struggle trying to tell people about what reflow2 actually is. It makes sense in my brain, but I have a hard time getting explaining what it is to somebody else. Secondly, people think it is "AI" and that I'm trying to get AI to do everything. It would be more accurately stated as a partnership between human, AI, and a graph. We've discussed this in the design a long time ago, but much of why I created this was to mitigate some of the shortcomings of AI (can hallucinate, can be over confident, etc). I think in explaining what reflow2 is, we need to explain the partnership between human, AI, and graph. Additionally, I think this could actually be used to help people collaborate effectively rather than stop people from communicating. My boss said something along the lines of "we're not trying to eliminate people or people collaborating". I think this stems from a misconception that reflow2 isn't AI and it isn't about replacing people. Anyways, really trying to start putting a cohesive story together of what reflow2 is and is-not."

ALREADY SETTLED, so not open here: the partnership itself. rule:reflow2-is-one-of-three-parts-and-does-not-compete-with-the-others (his words 2026-09-02): human supplies ideas and direction, the LLM reasoning and knowledge, the graph persistent memory and relationships; none replaces or competes with another. dec:three-party-checks (accepted 2026-07-19): "The LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides". docs/partnership.md maps each known LLM failure mode to its check. docs/vision.md: concept to operations, and "the user never has to know systems engineering". WHAT IS OPEN is how to TELL it.

ELEMENTS HE NAMED, none chosen as wording:
1. Why it exists: to mitigate the model's shortcomings (hallucination, overconfidence).
2. What it is: a partnership of human, AI and graph.
3. What it is not: AI doing everything, or a replacement for people.
4. What it is for between people: helping them collaborate rather than stopping them from communicating (his boss: "we're not trying to eliminate people or people collaborating").
5. One cohesive story, told as both what it is and what it is not.

WAYS TO TELL IT, none chosen:
(a) A pitch built on the three parts, one sentence each: who brings what, and who checks whom. A draft to react to, not chosen: "You decide; the AI drafts, asks and checks; the graph remembers what was decided and why, so the project's reasons outlive the chat, the model and the people who leave."
(b) An "is / is not" pair as the site's first screen.
(c) Each AI shortcoming beside the part that answers it, taken from docs/partnership.md. Making things up: the graph holds what was actually decided, by whom, and says when nothing matched. Overconfidence: every finding says whether it was measured or forecast, and only a named person settles intent. Forgetting: the record persists across sessions and models.
(d) Tell it through one design's walkthrough (dec:idea-how-does-the-site-show-what-reflow2-is-for-one-design-by-itself), with each step labelled by who does it: the person, the AI or the graph.
(e) Show two people and their agents on one design: every decision names who made it and when; a question goes to the person it belongs to; the record carries why, so the next conversation starts from it rather than replacing it.

ADDED THE SAME DAY, his words: "That might be a lot for one page, so may need to spread that out on 2 - 3 pages". One possible split, NOT chosen: (1) what it is and is not, the partnership, and why (the AI shortcomings and who checks whom); (2) one design from intent through to code and back (the walkthrough); (3) several people on one design (collaboration), with the hub as the step after. Counter, recorded beside it: each page is read again at every cut under req:every-release-brings-reflow2s-site-up-to-date-with-what-it-ships, and a reader who stops on the home page still has to meet the one-line version there. That argues for a short "is / is not" on the home page in any split.

ADDED THE SAME DAY, his words: "One other thing is that I think we explain it in simple terms and phrases - something that most non-technical people could go to and get a good idea of what it is without getting intimidated or bogged down by too much. Basically, I think the concepts of reflow2 should be easy to tell". So the story's reader is a non-technical person: plain words and short phrases, nothing that intimidates or bogs them down. The concepts themselves should be easy to tell. Counter, recorded beside it: reflow2's own vocabulary (graph, node, capability, drift, golden thread) is where a plain explanation is most easily lost, and the people who misread it as "AI" at work are engineers. One telling may not serve both. A plain first layer, with a deeper page for those who want it, is one way to keep both; it fits the 2-3 page split above. The vision already says "the user never has to know systems engineering", so a plain telling matches settled intent rather than diluting it.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-12 — promoted into: reflow2's site says, in plain words, what reflow2 is and is not, as a partnership in which a person decides, an AI drafts, asks and checks, and a graph remembers
properties.rationale:
Counter-arguments and costs, recorded beside the idea, not against it:

1. A CLAIM OF "PARTNERSHIP" IS EASY TO HEAR AS MARKETING. Readers believe a concrete case over a claim, which argues for (c), (d) or (e) over (a) alone. The rule itself came from a colleague saying a current model could design a small service in a few hours without reflow2, and Anthony agreed that was true for that case. An honest "is not" says WHEN reflow2 is not needed: short, one-person, one-sitting work. Saying so is also what makes the rest credible.

2. "IT IS NOT AI" NEEDS CARE. reflow2 itself runs no model: measured 2026-10-12, no crate depends on a model library. But it is used through an AI agent, and the site says "a graph any AI agent can read". The accurate line is that reflow2 is the record and the checks that a person and an AI work against. It is not the AI.

3. COLLABORATION MUST MATCH WHAT EACH ROUTE DELIVERS. Named authorship, dated decisions and questions routed to a person work everywhere. Claims ("I'm working on this part") persist on a served design (flo2.io or --serve-shared) but not under --call, where each call is a fresh session (fact:recurrence-a-door-call-cannot-hold-a-seat-a-claim-or-a-writes-for-2026-10-05). reflow2 also gives people no channel to talk to each other (dec:idea-reflow2-has-multi-seat-state-and-no-multi-seat-channel), which supports his boss's point: the conversation stays between people, and the graph gives it a memory. A story told at work, where he uses --call, should not promise what --call does not do.

4. COST: (a) and (b) are words on the existing home page. (c) reuses docs/partnership.md. (d) is the walkthrough already recorded. (e) needs an example with two people, which the Gearheads (a team) can carry. Each page added is read again at every release under req:every-release-brings-reflow2s-site-up-to-date-with-what-it-ships.

5. AUDIENCE AT WORK: engineers and scientists may hear "a traceable record of requirements, decisions and evidence that an AI assistant keeps current and a person approves" better than "AI", because it starts from what they already do.
